note: The Assistant Fishing Guide Training Manual (John, 2026-11-16): an audio companion to the book, fifteen short lessons read by the book's narrator (Brian, ElevenLabs) straight to the listener as a trainee, quoting Uncle Dan's sayings from data/quotes.json. The scripts are data/manual/<id>.txt (plain paragraphs; '[pause]' is two seconds of silence after a quiz question). scripts/narrate.mjs manual <n|all> makes the audio; lesson 1 is public/audio/tm-01.mp3 (free), lessons 2 to 15 are served from R2 to purchase-key holders. No sizes, seasons or bag limits are spoken; crew learn beside an adult captain. 'minutes' is filled in by the narration run (at the player's 1.1x).
title: The Assistant Fishing Guide Training Manual
subtitle: A listening companion to Escape to Lostman’s River
intro: Fifteen short lessons in what an assistant fishing guide has to know: the boat, the sky, the fish, the rigs, the guests and the hose. Read by the voice that reads the book, straight to you, with three questions at the end of nearly every one. Answer them out loud.

lessons.title: Welcome aboard, trainee
lessons.open: The Assistant Fishing Guide Training Manual. Lesson one. Welcome aboard, trainee.
lessons.blurb: The job you’re training for, how the manual works, and Uncle Dan’s five rules.

lessons.title: Boat words, and the morning checklist
lessons.open: Lesson two. Boat words, and the morning checklist.
lessons.blurb: Bow, stern, port and starboard, and the seven things a guide checks before the key turns.

lessons.title: Waking the engine, and the rules of the road
lessons.open: Lesson three. Waking the engine, and the rules of the road.
lessons.blurb: The tell-tale stream, red right returning, and why your wake is your business.

do.label: Learn the Boat: markers and manners

lessons.title: Reading the water, and getting unstuck
lessons.open: Lesson four. Reading the water, and getting unstuck.
lessons.blurb: Color, birds and bends, and the three-step drill for the day you run aground.

lessons.title: The mate’s jobs: anchor, dock, bait and ice
lessons.open: Lesson five. The mate’s jobs: the anchor, the dock, the bait and the ice.
lessons.blurb: Making the boat stop where the captain wants it, and keeping the bait alive and the catch cold.

do.label: Learn the Boat: anchoring and docking

lessons.title: Sun, storms and the sky
lessons.open: Lesson six. Sun, storms, and the sky.
lessons.blurb: Reading the clouds, counting the thunder, beating the heat, and the two jobs if someone goes over the side.

do.label: Learn the Boat: before you leave the dock

lessons.title: Know your fish: the six that matter
lessons.open: Lesson seven. Know your fish, part one. The six that matter.
lessons.blurb: Snook, tarpon, redfish, seatrout, snapper and grouper, described so you can see them with your eyes shut.

lessons.title: Know your fish: the rest of the river
lessons.open: Lesson eight. Know your fish, part two. The rest of the river.
lessons.blurb: The look-alikes, the bait thieves, and the ones to keep your fingers away from.

lessons.title: The neighbors
lessons.blurb: Manatees, dolphins, alligators, snakes and pelicans, and the manners that go with each.

lessons.title: Keeper or release?
lessons.blurb: How to measure a fish, what a slot is, where the real rules come from, and how to let one go.

lessons.title: Finding the fish
lessons.blurb: Six kinds of spot, six signs of fish, and why the tide matters more than either.

lessons.title: Rig it right
lessons.blurb: Seven rules, eight rigs, and one knot to learn with your fingers.

lessons.title: The bite, the fight and the net
lessons.open: Lesson thirteen. The bite, the fight, and the net.
lessons.blurb: Five ways to set a hook, how to fight a fish, and which end goes in the net first.

lessons.title: Your guests
lessons.blurb: The hard part: people. Names, sunscreen, hooks, slow days, and never taking the rod.

lessons.title: The end of the day, and the big one
lessons.open: Lesson fifteen. The end of the day, and the big one.
lessons.blurb: The ramp, the hose, the nine-step list, and what it takes to earn the big one.
